topic_name: Audio playback stalls after seeking or scrubbing
summary: Three tutors report audio playback that stops or stalls after seeking, scrubbing or jumping back, on AUD-741, AUD-754 and AUD-768.

severity.rationale: Supported rubric signals: signal:HIGH[3] Three tutors report playback stopping or stalling after seeking on AUD-741, AUD-754 and AUD-768.

affected_reporters.basis: Distinct authors whose own cited message reports the problem; other participants are not counted.

recommended_action.draft_text:
Audio playback stalls after seeking or scrubbing (three tutor reports, audio_pilot_17). Please check the player's seek handling.
- AUD-741, Firefox 132.0.2: sound stops after dragging the waveform back to the start, clock stays at 0:00; reopening restores playback until the next seek.
- AUD-754, Chrome 131.0.6778.85: after moving the scrubber the play icon changes but the clock never advances; a QA tutor reproduced it, and the downloaded WAV plays normally.
- AUD-768, Firefox 132.0.2: endless spinner after jump-back, after playback had worked.
The cause is not confirmed. Please say if you need more steps or task details.
recommended_action.scope_note: Covers only the three seek-related player reports; the cause is not confirmed. Reproduction steps are as the tutors described them.
recommended_action.label: Report a technical issue to engineering
recommended_action.instruction: Report one scoped technical issue to engineering covering AUD-741, AUD-754 and AUD-768, with browser versions and the reported steps.

reasoning: What the evidence shows: A tutor reports that on AUD-741 in Firefox 132.0.2 the sound stops after dragging the waveform back to the start with the time display at 0:00, that it played the first time, and that reopening restores it until they seek again. A tutor reports that on AUD-754 in Chrome 131.0.6778.85 reloading gives one listen, and after moving the scrubber the play triangle changes but the clock never advances. A tutor reports an endless spinner after using jump-back on AUD-768 in Firefox 132.0.2, after playback had already worked. A QA tutor reports reproducing the stuck clock on AUD-754 and says the downloaded WAV plays normally. A QA tutor asks the thread starter for the task ID and browser build, saying a second reproduction is needed before filing; the tutor then gives AUD-741 and Firefox 132.0.2. The team lead tells the thread starter, in the AUD-768 thread, to keep the affected task open and add browser and task details to one report. Current audio incident triage guidance says that for a reproducible player freeze after seeking, task IDs, browser versions and reproduction steps are collected and one scoped engineering incident is sent for the affected player reports.
